title: FDA reminder to avoid concomitant use of Plavix (clopidogrel) and omeprazole
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, posted 27 October 2010
result: FDA continues to warn against concomitant use of clopidogrel and omeprazole because co-administration can significantly reduce levels of the active metabolite of clopidogrel and its antiplatelet activity; the warning was added to the Plavix label in November 2009. The recommendation applies only to omeprazole, not to all PPIs, because PPIs differ in inhibition of CYP2C19; pantoprazole, a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, may be an alternative.
